Title: Scientex to acquire 70pct interest in China's Mintpack for RM102mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Scientex Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd (SPAK), has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a 70 per cent stake in China-based Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co., Ltd. ("Mintpack").
The proposed acquisition involves a purchase consideration of RMB167.3 million, approximately RM101.5 million, said Scientex in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday.
The agreement was signed with Tan Cui Fang, and Hunan Changcheng Tianyi Information Technology Co., Ltd. Tan is the founder of both Mintpack and Tianyi.
Upon the completion of the transaction, Mintpack will become an indirect subsidiary of Scientex, while Tianyi will retain the remaining 30 per cent equity interest.
Incorporated in July 2015, Mintpack operates from the Xiangtan Economic and Technological Development Zone in Hunan, China.
The company specializes in the manufacturing of high-quality flexible plastic packaging, including flexible plastic bags and roll films.
Scientex views the acquisition as a strategic avenue to expand the group's consumer packaging footprint into China.
The deal secures the group an established local manufacturing platform and customer base in China, directly complementing Scientex's existing consumer packaging operations.
By leveraging Mintpack's capabilities and market presence, Scientex aims to develop new multinational client relationships and expand its reach into new export markets.
The consolidation of Mintpack's earnings and operations will provide the enlarged Scientex Group with increased production capacity and a diversified portfolio across regional and global markets.
The RM101.5 million purchase consideration was negotiated on a willing-buyer willing-seller basis. It factors in Mintpack's historical financial performance, its future growth prospects, and its audited net assets of RMB119.5 million as of Dec 31, 2025.
Scientex will finance the acquisition utilizing a combination of internally generated funds and bank borrowings.
The acquisition is not expected to have any material effect on Scientex's earnings per share, net assets per share, gearing, share capital, or substantial shareholders' shareholdings for the financial year ending July 31, 2027.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances and subject to all relevant approvals being obtained, Scientex expects to complete the acquisition of Mintpack by the end of 2026.

Title: Why do so many Malaysians ride motorcycles?
Article:
FOR many riders, the motorcycle is solving a practical problem. It gets them to work affordably, reliably and on time.
The challenge is that the mobility solution millions depend on is also the mode carrying Malaysia's greatest road-safety exposure.
The scale alone tells us motorcycles are not a marginal transport issue. In 2024, 78.1 per cent of Malaysian households owned a motorcycle.
Our preliminary research found more than 13.6 million motorcycle registrations between 2000 and mid-2026, including 655,837 new registrations in 2024.
It has become deeply embedded in Malaysian mobility. But not every motorcyclist is riding for the same reason.
A factory worker travelling before the first bus arrives faces a very different problem from a professional riding into Kuala Lumpur to avoid congestion.
A rural household using a motorcycle to reach a school or clinic has different needs from a university student. A p-hailing rider is different again. For that rider, the motorcycle is not simply transport.
It is the tool that earns the income. Our research identifies industrial and shift workers, delivery riders, congestion-avoidance commuters, rural users, students and early-career workers. Their travel patterns and realistic alternatives differ.
That distinction matters because one policy response cannot work equally well for all of them.
For many workers, the attraction of the motorcycle is easy to understand. Public transport may exist within the wider city, but that does not necessarily mean it connects a person's home to the workplace at the right time.
Our research examined illustrative commuting scenarios involving industrial areas in Klang, Rawang, Senai, Bayan Lepas and Pasir Gudang.
In those examples, public transport journeys could take roughly 50 to 67 minutes longer in one direction than travelling by motorcycle because of indirect routes, transfers, service frequency and weak first- and last-mile connections.
They expose an important issue: people count time spent waiting, walking and changing services.
They consider whether the bus arrives before their shift, whether the last service operates when they finish work, and whether they can reach the final kilometer.
A cheap journey is not necessarily a practical journey if it takes twice as long.
This does not mean motorcycles are always the better mode. It means that, under certain Malaysian conditions, choosing a motorcycle can be an entirely rational decision.
And that is where the national dilemma begins. The safety burden is severe. The research records 6,443 road deaths in 2023, of which 4,489, or 69.4 per cent, involved motorcyclists.
The employment dimension makes this even more serious. PERKESO data examined in the study recorded 46,542 commuting accidents in 2025, representing 50.9 per cent of occupational accident claims in that dataset.
More than 80 per cent of commuting fatalities recorded there involved motorcyclists.
When the journey to work becomes one of the most dangerous parts of the working day, motorcycle safety is no longer only a traffic issue. It becomes a workforce issue.
[[nid:1543981]]
That does not mean rider behaviour should be ignored. Speeding matters. Helmets matter. Licensing, vehicle condition and enforcement matter.
But so do road design, traffic speeds, public transport accessibility, working hours and the amount of time riders are exposed to traffic.
The objective should not be to replace rider-blaming with system-blaming, but to understand the whole system.
Malaysia already has useful experience. The country pioneered dedicated motorcycle facilities on corridors such as the Federal Highway and KESAS.
Research cited in our study found meaningful safety gains from segregation, while also identifying weaknesses involving road geometry, barriers, drainage, lighting and the places where motorcycle lanes reconnect with mixed traffic.
The lesson is not simply to build more motorcycle lanes. The better question is where separation works, how it should be designed, and how the entire journey can be made safer.
Motorcycles and public transport should not always be treated as competitors. Some motorcycle trips could shift entirely to buses or rail. Others may be shortened.
Could we make it easier for someone to ride three kilometres to a station instead of 30 kilometres to work?
Our research raises this possibility through better motorcycle-to-transit integration, including secure parking and safer access to stations.
Other journeys will remain motorcycle-dependent, especially for commercial riders and people living or working in places with limited alternatives. Those journeys must be made substantially safer.
This is why MYARTTE (MY Asean Road and Traffic Tech Expo) intends to convene a Roundtable on Motorcycle Mobility in Malaysia.
The purpose is not to begin with a predetermined solution or assign blame. It is to bring government agencies, researchers, industry, employers, operators and riders together around three basic questions.
Why are Malaysians riding? Which motorcycle journeys could realistically be replaced or shortened? How do we make the journeys that remain much safer?
No single agency controls all the factors involved. Transport planning, road engineering, enforcement, vehicle standards, public transport, urban development, employment and social protection all influence the outcome.
For many Malaysians, the motorcycle is not the problem. It is the answer to a problem: how to reach work, education and opportunity at a price and within a time they can afford.
The challenge for Malaysia is to provide better answers. We should continue asking how motorcyclists can ride more safely.
But if we are serious about reducing the human cost, we must also ask why so many Malaysians have to ride in the first place.
* The writer is founder & senior adviser, My Mobility Vision

Title: Missing Orang Asli woman found dead in Rompin swamp
Article:
ROMPIN: The search for a missing 73-year-old Orang Asli woman ended today when her body was found in a swampy area in Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, police said.
The remains of Kuang Poh,
who was last seen
leaving her home for a fishing trip on Sept 22, were found at 11.50am.
Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said search and rescue (SAR) team members found Kuang's decomposed remains about 500 metres from where she was last seen.
"SAR teams today focused on several areas within a five-kilometre radius of the settlement before her remains were spotted in an overgrown swampy area.
"The remains were taken to Rompin Hospital for a post-mortem examination at 1.05pm. The case has been classified as sudden death," he said in a statement today.
Kuang failed to return home after leaving for a fishing trip at about 3pm on Sept 22, prompting a relative to lodge a missing person report the following day.
Yesterday, Sharif Shai said the swampy terrain and the risk of
encountering wild animals
, including leopards, tigers and elephants, were among the challenges faced by SAR teams.

Title: PN seeks RoS clarification on use of coalition logo in Melaka election
Article:
KOTA BHARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has written to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) seeking clarification on whether it can use the coalition's logo in the Melaka election.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the letter was sent yesterday and the coalition was now awaiting a response.
"We have written to RoS to seek clarification on whether the Perikatan Nasional logo can be used in the Melaka election.
"We sent the letter yesterday, seeking clarification, so we will wait," he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after attending the presentation of state honours in conjunction with the 57th birthday celebrations of Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V at Istana Balai Besar here today.
Takiyuddin said PN had also sought clarification and details of a complaint lodged by Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) over alleged breaches of the coalition's constitution by its new leadership.
"Right now, we do not know. We have been asked to provide an explanation, but we do not even know what the complaint is. So, we are seeking clarification from RoS," he said.
Asked whether PN had other options for a logo, Takiyuddin said it was not an issue as any party could use another party's logo but that would be discussed later.
"There are many other options. In an election, any party can use another party's logo. Other parties can also use another party's logo.
"For example, in 2018, everyone used the PKR logo. Bersatu used it, DAP used it, so there is no problem. The logo is not an issue," he said.
On Sept 24, RoS was reported to have suspended all activities of PN.
In a statement, RoS said the suspension order was issued under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832) to safeguard the interests of the organisation from continuing to breach its rules.

Title: Vantris recorded RM75mil fourth-consecutive quarterly net profits in Q2
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vantris Energy Bhd reported net profit of RM75.3 million in the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27) – its fourth consecutive quarter in the black – despite registering lower revenue.
The turnaround from the corresponding quarter last year was driven by lower foreign exchange losses, the absence of a favourable insurance claim recorded in the previous corresponding quarter and lower finance costs following the completion of the company's restructuring exercise.
Revenue for the quarter fell 22.8 per cent to RM818 million from RM1.06 billion, mainly due to lower contributions from the engineering and construction (E&C) segment.
This drop stemmed from the group pivot towards service-centered, lower-risk activities and contracts featuring a more balanced risk exposure across Australia and Southeast Asia.
Compared with the preceding quarter ended April 30, 2026, Vantris' net profits was 93.6 per cent lower in the recently-concluded quarter, due to the absence of insurance claim proceeds recognised previously, as well as realised foreign exchange losses.
For the first half ended July 31, 2026, Vantris posted a net profit of RM221 million, compared with a net loss of RM708.7 million a year earlier, on 21.9 per cent lower revenue of RM1.46 billion.
The company's order book stood at RM7 billion as at July 31, up from RM5.9 billion in the first quarter, while its share of order books held through joint ventures and associates stood at RM2.7 billion.
Group chief executive officer Muhammad Zamri Jusoh said Vantris remained focused on converting its order book into consistent and profitable delivery.
"This quarter reflects continued progress in rebuilding a more sustainable operating performance. We remain focused on strengthening repeatable operating earnings through disciplined project execution, tight cost control and improved asset utilisation," he said.
The E&C segment delivered higher revenue quarter-on-quarter, supported by increased activity from ongoing projects and the commencement of new projects across Southeast Asia and Australia.
Key projects undertaken during the quarter included four decommissioning projects in Thailand and Australia.
The operations and maintenance (O&M) segment also recorded improved revenue in Q2 FY27 following the commencement of new subsea work orders.
Its order book stood around RM1.2 billion, with the segment focused on expanding its presence across Southeast Asia and securing contracts that support sustained, long-term utilisation of its assets.
Meanwhile, the drilling segment continued to contribute positively at the operating level, although revenue was lower than in Q1 FY27 due to reduced utilisation of two rigs during the transition between contracts.
Both rigs have since commenced new work, with the segment supported by sustained demand for its fleet and an order book of about RM2.3 billion.
Separately, Vantris said it was closely monitoring geopolitical developments, particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
While its direct exposure to the affected region remained limited, the company said management continued to assess potential impacts on its operations and supply chain, as well as broader market conditions.

Title: KLIA workers, community to get priority access during Sepang F1
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The movement of the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) community and airport workers to Terminal 1, Terminal 2 and the cargo and Free Commercial Zone (FCZ) areas will be prioritised during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said access would be maintained via Lebuh Madani, Charterfield Roundabout and Jalan CTA 2 during the championship at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2 to 4.
"Special access will also be provided for Friday prayers on Oct 2, from 12.30pm to 2.30pm, towards Sultan Abdul Samad KLIA Mosque," he said in a statement.
Shazeli said SIC would have parking capacity for 9,000 cars across 17 parking lots, with spaces allocated at any one time according to designated categories.
To facilitate visitor movement, free shuttle bus and e-hailing services would also be provided from various locations to SIC.
"A total of 95 MyRapid buses will operate from 4 main hubs — KLIA Terminal 2 Level 1, Mitsui KLIA/De-Village, Persiaran Milenia 2 and Bandar Baru Enstek.
"Another 50 tour buses, in collaboration with e-hailing company Grab, will operate from the Long Term Car Park (LTCP)," he said.
Shazeli added that there would also be 200 Grab e-hailing passes for passenger drop-off zones at SIC and LTCP, as well as 100 Prestige Lane passes for passenger pick-ups from selected hotels.
"Visitors should not park their vehicles on road shoulders to ensure smooth traffic flow.
"Summonses and towing action could be taken against vehicles obstructing traffic, with tow trucks provided in the area," he said.
Shazeli said motorcycles would not be allowed to enter the SIC area and could instead be parked at designated motorcycle parking areas.
"Members of the public and the KLIA community are also advised to plan their journeys early, comply with instructions from personnel and refer to digital information boards around the circuit," he said.

Title: French teens clash with police as school blockades intensify
Article:
PARIS: French teenagers on Tuesday set fire to rubbish bins and hurled projectiles in clashes with police, as they kept up a blockade of some high schools demanding better conditions at their establishments but which has angered the government.
High school students have since last week staged protests outside their schools over grievances including timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers as well as overheated classrooms in the wake of the recent heatwaves.
The movement in the lycees, which handle the final years of school in France, started in the Ile-de-France region around Paris, where blockades in some 10 schools were reported by education authorities Tuesday. It has now spread to other cities nationwide.
Masked students gathered outside the Lycee Cesar Baggio in Lille, in northern France, setting bins on fire, an AFP photographer reported.
Bus shelters and advertising billboards were vandalised, with bottles, paving stones and various objects hurled at police who responded by firing tear gas.
Teens piled up dozens of bins to prevent entrance to the Lycee Gabriel Guist'hau in the western city of Nantes, while in Paris there was an uneasy standoff between 30 students and a contingent of police at the Arago school.
Similar actions were also reported in cities including Marseille in the south, Bordeaux in the west and Lyon in the southeast.
At the Lamartine school in Paris around 80 students gathered outside brandishing slogans including "more hours of lessons than sleep" and "8am to 6pm, are we pupils or under arrest?"
There were tense scenes at the Lycee Brequigny in the northwestern city of Rennes – Brittany's largest high school – where around a hundred students hurled projectiles at the building, an AFP video journalist said.
The actions came as unions planned a day of nationwide demonstrations and also strikes over the budget of Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, a close ally of President Emmanuel Macron.
[[nid:1543953]]
Tens of thousands were expected to rally in Paris and other cities, with teachers and fire services striking nationwide although with public transport not badly affected.
"The anger is immense. I warn the government – it must address the demands and revise the draft budget, which is dangerous for the country and is driving us straight into the wall of recession at 200 kilometres an hour," the head of the hardline CGT union Sophie Binet told BFM TV.
A 17-year-old pupil at the Lamartine school, who asked not to be named, said they had been angered by a lack of resources, overheated classrooms and overly congested timetables.
"We are also there to support our teachers who have a crazy amount of work compared to what they earn," she told AFP.
Lecornu on Monday said any escalation of demonstrations at high schools would be "irresponsible" and lashed out at the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party for encouraging the protests.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 164 arrests took place on Monday and 180 schools were affected, adding: "We cannot tolerate excesses."
In the low-income Paris suburb of Seine-Saint-Denis, the district's LFI mayor Bally Bagayoko joined a protest of hundreds of students at the Lycee Paul-Eluard.
Leading students in a rendition of the Marseillaise, he described the protests as "completely legitimate" and complained low income areas received less resources than higher income ones.
"We, the children of the suburbs, are abandoned and neglected," said 16-year-old Victoire, a student at the school, denouncing conditions at the establishment as "unsanitary."

Title: Undocumented Bajau Laut youths face exploitation in Sabah
Article:
SEMPORNA: Undocumented Bajau Laut youths in Sabah face exploitation and limited employment opportunities as changes to their traditional sea-based livelihoods add to their challenges.
The Bajau Laut are a traditionally sea-based community in Sabah, with some members among the state's undocumented population, lacking official documents.
When Bob was sexually harassed by a foreign guest while working in the hospitality sector, the 21-year-old did not report the incident.
Instead, he quit his job.
"I panicked. I left my job. I didn't tell my boss because I was afraid.
"I didn't have any documents to report. I didn't want the problem to get worse," said Bob, a pseudonym used to protect his identity.
Bob, who was born in a village and grew up without official documents, said his parents had little education and did not know how to obtain them.
Since turning 18, Bob has been taking part-time jobs in Semporna, including as a tour guide, lifeguard, food server and hotel housekeeper.
He said he also faced disputes over his wages, including one occasion when his daily pay was reduced from RM30 to RM25 after colleagues described him as lazy and slow.
"I could not dispute it as I am not in the position to argue as I may be subjected to arrest due to being undocumented," he said.
He said he was paid in cash because he did not have a bank account.
[[nid:1543947]]
Undocumented and vulnerable
For 18-year-old Aisah, a third-generation Bajau Laut, the problem begins even earlier — with the changing relationship between her community and the sea.
She said the ocean had long been more than a source of food, serving as a means of livelihood and sustaining generations of her family and community.
"The ocean, which was once our source of livelihood, now seems to belong only to people with documents.
"I wished that others could share the ocean resources with us," she said.
Their experiences come against a wider backdrop of undocumented populations in Sabah, whose size remains difficult to establish.
A United Nations research paper series on Sabah's undocumented population noted that there was no official, authoritative estimate of the number of undocumented people in the state and that its research did not attempt to produce one.
The paper defines the undocumented population as people living in Sabah who lack papers that confer identity.
The research found that the undocumented population in Sabah is ethnically diverse and should not simply be understood as a migrant population.
It said about 30 per cent of the undocumented population had origins in Sabah, including indigenous people and the Bajau Laut, while many of those who came from elsewhere had arrived decades ago and had remained in Sabah for generations.
It described these populations as well integrated into Sabah's social and economic structures, with undocumented people often indistinct from citizens. It said they were largely settled rather than transient populations.
[[nid:1543946]]
Changing livelihoods
Universiti Malaysia Sabah Social Sciences and Humanities Faculty lecturer Associate Professor Wan Shawaluddin Wan Hassan, who has researched the Bajau Laut community in Semporna, said increased maritime security measures, marine conservation restrictions and declining marine resources had reduced the areas where some community members could fish and move.
He said the Bajau Laut had traditionally maintained a maritime lifestyle, travelling between waters around Sabah, the Philippines and Indonesia in boats known as lepa.
"They used to sustain their lives by obtaining food from the sea and trading seafood for cassava.
"However, after the Lahad Datu intrusion in 2013, increased maritime security measures by Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia have reduced the areas where the Bajau Laut can move and look for food," he said.
Wan Shawaluddin said their traditional knowledge of the sea, including seafaring and freediving skills, remained valuable and could potentially be incorporated into the local economy.
Bajau Laut freedivers are known for their ability to dive to considerable depths and locate high-value marine species such as lobsters.
Wan Shawaluddin said there was potential to provide members of the community with skills and opportunities to enter other sectors, including tourism and other parts of Sabah's economy.
However, he cautioned that any transition away from a sea-based lifestyle would require time and support.
"Without education, they can be exploited in many ways that they may not be aware of.
"By working and earning an income, it could improve their lives and perhaps enable them to send their children to alternative schools," he said.
He said efforts to support the community should also recognise its cultural identity and traditional knowledge rather than simply seeking to move its members into land-based employment.
Wan Shawaluddin said without proper guidance and support, attempts to integrate the community into the mainstream economy could expose its members to further exploitation.
[[nid:1543945]]
Advocates for Non-Discrimination and Access to Knowledge founder Anne Baltazar said people get exploited when they are vulnerable.
"We have to reduce vulnerabilities by increasing access to basic services such as legal documentation, education and healthcare.
"We also need systems in place, both by the government and civil society organisations, to protect undocumented persons, especially children."
Anne also called for greater awareness of birth registration, which is meant for everyone regardless of their status.
"Birth registration does not automatically mean citizenship, but it creates an official record that can help establish identity, parentage and possible nationality links, which then helps determine the appropriate documentation or protection pathway."

Title: [UPDATED] 'Where do we put them?': Anwar defends Myanmar talks, demands safety guarantees for refugees
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended Malaysia's engagement with Myanmar, saying calls to simply "not send them back" offer no solution for the hundreds of thousands of Myanmar refugees in the country.
He said Malaysia was seeking security guarantees for any returns, which was why Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing had been invited for talks.
"I have received several views on their concerns about being sent home. That is why, in our negotiations, we bind all of this.
"It is easy for them (the critics) to say, 'Don't send them back.' Then where do we put the thousands? What we want now are conditions to ensure there is security. That is why we invited him (Min Aung Hlaing) to negotiate," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the inaugural Professionals Conference & Exhibition (Profex 2026) at the KLGCC Convention Centre here.
Anwar said Malaysia's position was to protect the welfare and human rights of refugees, adding that he did not think it was fair to condemn the government for taking the initiative.
He rejected suggestions that Malaysia was simply pushing the refugees back.
"No, it's not true. We, of course, negotiate. We are quite stringent in our conditions, although it's their citizens," he said.
Anwar said he was glad Min Aung Hlaing had accepted the invitation, adding that any decision would have to be deliberated jointly by the Malaysian and Myanmar governments.
He said protests without proposing solutions would only complicate matters, adding that continued engagement was necessary as the problem had persisted for decades and was worsening.
He also questioned what alternative critics and non-governmental organisations were proposing.
"What is the solution as being suggested by some and many of these organisations? Keep them here? Now 200,000 or 300,000 (refugees), just keep them?" he asked.
Anwar also criticised Western countries that he said were censuring Malaysia over its approach, referring to their response to Israel's actions.
Thousands of people have fled Myanmar since the 2021 military coup, which triggered a nationwide armed conflict.
The crisis followed the military's 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State, which forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.
The Rohingya have faced longstanding discrimination and are largely denied citizenship under Myanmar's 1982 citizenship law.
As of February, Malaysia was hosting about 193,800 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya and Chin, according to UNHCR data. Activists have said the actual number could be higher as many refugees remain unregistered.

Title: Cocaine evidence missing from Fiji court was swapped out for flour, media say
Article:
SYDNEY: Several kilogrammes of cocaine held as evidence in a major Fiji drug case have gone missing from a court, police said on Tuesday, with media saying the drug, valued at about US$31 million, was swapped out for flour.
The drug exhibits stolen from the High Court in Suva, the capital of the Pacific island nation, amounted to nearly 40 kg, media said.
Police began investigating after the Sept 15 discovery of the theft of seven out of 39 cocaine bars from an evidence room.
Forensic tests on the remaining drugs confirmed that exhibits had been tampered with, police said in a statement on Tuesday, adding that they would question a person of interest who was allegedly overseas.
"The exhibits were all tampered with and the investigation is focused on those directly charged with the management of the exhibits at the High Court registry," police said.
The Fiji Village news outlet said the remaining 32 bars had been filled with flour.
Those responsible for the theft would face the full force of the law, said Justice Minister Siromi Turaga.
"It's shocking ... no one will be spared," he told news outlet Fiji One, adding it was not the first such instance. It was not immediately clear what punishment offenders face.
Media said the cocaine was seized from Fiji-Canadian national Joshua Aziz Rahman in 2019 and stored at the court as evidence while he appealed against his 2021 conviction and sentence.
Fiji police have said cases involving drugs such as methamphetamine and cocaine have surged since 2018.
In 2024, the United Nations said Fiji had emerged as a regional hub for drug trafficking in the Pacific.
The number of drug arrests, mainly linked to methamphetamine, more than tripled in 2023, it added in a report.

Title: German security agencies face dilemma after victories for far right and far left
Article:
THIS month's victories for far-right and far-left parties in German state elections have intensified official debate over whether security authorities can restrict secret information that might be passed on to Russia or criminal groups.
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which came close to winning an absolute majority in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sept 6, and the far-left Left Party, which came first in the capital Berlin on Sept 20, could both pose risks, senior figures in the ruling coalition say.
In Germany's federal system, states have their own domestic intelligence agencies under local government control, which share information with each other and operate with the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV).
Politicians from rival parties and former security officials have expressed fears that if the agencies come under the authority of ministers from the far right or far left, confidential information could leak either to Moscow or, in the case of Berlin, to groups investigated over suspicions of organised crime links.
"This concerns information relating to organised crime – that would be an issue in Berlin," said Alexander Hoffmann, head of the parliamentary group of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU).
"And it's about issues concerning Russia – that would be Saxony-Anhalt," he said.
The AfD rejects accusations from rival parties that it is effectively allied to Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying that it seeks only to avoid war and opposes Germany providing military support for Ukraine.
An AfD spokesperson said the government was "clutching at straws in an attempt to discredit us in the eyes of the electorate."
"It is telling that we have been confronted with such speculation and accusations for many years, yet the other side has failed to produce a single piece of evidence," the spokesperson said in an emailed statement.
The Left Party did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
But party leaders have previously said they considered as unacceptable any association with what German police identify as clan structures within the Kurdish, Lebanese and Palestinian communities in Berlin involved in organised crime.
The accusations of links to such groups are often intertwined with accusations of antisemitism, which the party also says it firmly rejects.
The discussion over restricting confidential information has been underway ever since opinion polls pointed to a possible victory for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, where the local branch of the party is designated as right-wing extremist by the local office of the domestic intelligence agency.
Hendrik Wuest, the CDU state premier of North Rhine-Westphalia, earlier this month called for a special federal and state committee to be set up to consider how to deal with the issue of information-sharing with an AfD-led government.
[[nid:1543915]]
"Of course, preparations are under way – but people are still waiting to see what happens, because it isn't even clear whether the AfD and The Left will form governments at all," said one security official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Despite coming first in the election in Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD fell short of the absolute majority it would need to govern alone, and its coalition options are restricted because the other main parties have all ruled out cooperating with it.
The Left Party is, however, likely to try to form a coalition with the centre-left Social Democrats and the environmental Greens, but both parties have demanded that it take action to eliminate antisemitism from its ranks.
Several of the AfD's state party branches have been designated as far-right extremist groups by domestic security authorities, prompting the AfD in turn to accuse the intelligence services of political interference.
Officials are also concerned that security officials involved in investigating the AfD could be targeted by a future AfD-led administration.
Tensions between political parties and the security services have surfaced from time to time in recent decades - but the idea of systematic exclusion from information sharing underlines the gravity of the division.
Along with the main domestic security agency, the BfV, other security services and state governments are now considering restrictions, although security officials say they would not want to cut off all information-sharing, citing issues including indications of potential terrorist attacks.
Left Party representatives say terms such as "clan-related crime" often stigmatise entire ethnic communities and say that contacts with local residents do not imply support for criminal activity.
Like the AfD, it has long been suspicious of the BfV. The Left Party's Berlin campaign programme called for the Berlin state agency to be abolished and replaced with "a transparent, democratically controlled body that is close to the people."
However one Left Party member of the federal parliament has acknowledged social media contacts with a member of an extended family in Berlin accused of involvement with criminal groups and said he would "take the time to dispel any doubts" and "review my communication style."
"There is absolutely no justification for elected representatives having contacts with individuals associated with organised crime," Ferat Kocak said in a post on the social media platform X.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Heavy vehicles to be diverted around Sepang during F1 Bahrain GP weekend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Heavy vehicles and lorries will be diverted at eight main checkpoints around the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026 from Oct 2 to 4.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the diversion would be carried out by the Selangor police contingent's Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID), together with the Road Transport Department (RTD).
"Exceptions will only be given to critical cargo that has made prior arrangements.
"Among the checkpoints are Masjid Roundabout, Jalan KLIA S8, Jalan B48, Persiaran Teknologi 1 and 2, and Jalan Besar Salak," he said in a statement.
Shazeli said TEID would also operate five main screening locations for ticket and vehicle-pass checks.
They are Kota Warisan towards Labohan Dagang, KLIA Toll Plaza, the KLIA 1 exit towards Masjid Roundabout, before Masjid Roundabout and the Jalan Kuarters intersection at the Enstek traffic lights.
"TEID personnel will be deployed from 8am to 11pm for macro traffic control, patrols and enforcement during the championship.
"The operation will cover three zones: the inner zone within two kilometres of SIC, the middle zone between three and five kilometres, and the outer zone covering areas six kilometres and beyond," he said.
Shazeli said the public should comply with instructions from personnel and refer to digital information boards provided around the circuit to facilitate traffic movement.
The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026 will be held at SIC from Oct 2 to 4, with the main race scheduled for Oct 4.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Why single out Loke when corruption is real problem, asks Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has questioned why Anthony Loke was being singled out over his offer to resign as transport minister.
Anwar said corruption and plunder were the nation's real issues, rather than Loke's resignation.
"This issue of Anthony Loke... what is the problem? He only gave the letter yesterday.
"What is the problem with Anthony Loke? The problem is corruption. The problem is robbery and plunder.
"That issue is not being raised, but people keep raising that he should resign. Why? Are those who plunder being told to resign?" he told reporters at the inaugural Professionals Conference & Exhibition (Profex 2026) at the KLGCC Convention Centre here.
Anwar defended Loke's record in the Cabinet, saying he saw no fault in his work and would discuss the matter with him directly.
"What is the problem with his work? His work is good! His performance as a minister is very good!" he said.
Anwar said the country had to decide how it wanted to deal with the issue.
"I want to ask seriously, what is this country going to do (on corruption)? So, the issue of corruption we erase, and we discuss Anthony Loke being told to resign," he said.
Earlier today, Loke said he had submitted his resignation letter to the prime minister, with the
resignation
to take effect when former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returns home to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
Loke, who is DAP secretary-general, said he met Anwar yesterday, during which the prime minister asked him to remain in the cabinet for the time being.
On Sept 19, Loke signalled his intention to
step down
as transport minister after the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib would serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to a RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 822 police, RTD personnel deployed for F1 Bahrain GP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 822 police and Road Transport Department (RTD) personnel will be deployed for security and traffic management during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026 at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 2 to 4.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the deployment comprised 756 policemen including 391 general-duty personnel and 365 traffic personnel, supported by 66 RTD officers.
"The overall security operation will run from 8am to 11pm daily, while racing activities at the circuit will take place from 9am to 6pm, with the main race scheduled for Oct 4.
"Security measures will also cover concerts by Axwell on Oct 3 and Martin Garrix on Oct 4, both scheduled from 7pm to 10pm at the SIC helipad for valid ticket holders," he said in a statement.
Shazeli said the Selangor police contingent's Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) would deploy personnel from 8am to 11pm for macro traffic control, patrols and enforcement.
"The deployment will be divided into three main zones. The inner zone, covering areas within two kilometres, includes Jalan Pekeliling, Jalan Kuarters, Jalan Besar Salak and Jalan B48 Kampung Chincang.
"The middle zone, covering three to five kilometres, includes the KLIA Expressway, Jalan Labohan Dagang, Jalan Pekeliling and Jalan KLIA 1.
"The outer zone, covering areas six kilometres and beyond, includes access routes around the KLIA Toll Plaza, PLUS, ELITE, Nilai and Jalan Labu," he said.
Shazeli said the integrated security and traffic management plan was being implemented to maintain public order and ensure smooth movement throughout the race weekend.

Title: S&P reaffirms Malaysia's A- rating, stable outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: S&P Global Ratings has reaffirmed Malaysia's sovereign credit rating at 'A-' with a "Stable" outlook, citing the economy's resilience, diversification and sustained growth momentum.
The Finance Ministry said S&P also pointed to Malaysia's gradual fiscal consolidation, strong monetary policy flexibility and historically supportive external position.
The "Stable" outlook reflects S&P's expectation that Malaysia's growth momentum and current policy environment will support steady fiscal performance over the next two to three years, the ministry said in a statement today.
S&P expects Malaysia's economy to expand 5.5 per cent in 2026, following 5.2 per cent growth in 2025 and 5.7 per cent year-on-year expansion in the first half of this year.
It forecasts average annual growth of 5 per cent over 2026-2029, while Malaysia's 10-year weighted-average real GDP per capita growth is estimated at 3.7 per cent, above the global median for countries at similar income levels.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the rating reaffirmation reflected the government's efforts to balance fiscal consolidation with economic growth and household protection.
"Since the launch of Ekonomi Madani, we have pursued reforms gradually and sequentially, balancing the need to strengthen our fiscal foundations with the imperative to sustain growth and protect the rakyat from external volatility," he said in the statement.
S&P attributed Malaysia's resilience partly to stronger electrical and electronics and semiconductor shipments amid the global artificial intelligence investment cycle, higher energy exports and resilient household consumption.
The agency said Malaysia's established E&E ecosystem, alongside initiatives under Ekonomi Madani and the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, could support longer-term growth.
It also identified Malaysia as Southeast Asia's leading data-centre investment destination, with an estimated RM386 billion in cumulative investment between 2021 and mid-2026.
S&P recognised Malaysia's continued fiscal consolidation, with the fiscal deficit narrowing to 3.7 per cent of GDP in 2025 from 6.4 per cent in 2021.
It said the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2023 provides a framework for stronger fiscal governance, transparency and risk management, while noting its bipartisan support.
Malaysia's external position remains another source of resilience, backed by a diversified export base and more than two decades of current account surpluses.
S&P expects the current account surplus to stabilise at about 1.8 per cent of GDP over the next three years.
It also assessed Bank Negara Malaysia as having significant independence and strong monetary policy credibility, with inflation expectations remaining well anchored.
Anwar said the government would continue reforms under Ekonomi Madani and the 13th Malaysia Plan, focusing on fiscal sustainability, productivity and competitiveness.
He said the 2027 Budget, to be tabled on Oct 9, would build on those reforms to translate stronger growth into higher incomes, better opportunities and improved living standards.

Title: Myanmar airstrike toll hits 50 as families gather dead
Article:
KYAUKTAW: Families searched for bodies on Tuesday around a charred market in western Myanmar after a military airstrike killed 50 people, one of the deadliest recent bombardments in the civil war.
Witnesses say the military's air force raided the riverside commercial hub in Kyauktaw town in western Rakhine state around midday (0530 GMT) on Monday.
"It breaks my heart to see our people dying," said Aung Chay, still hunting for the remains of his brother-in-law he believes was killed in the attack.
"Civilians are being unjustly murdered, and I can't bear to watch it," the 49-year-old said. "I feel deeply pained and incredibly angry."
It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the attack, which had an initial reported death toll of around 30.
"The death toll has reached 50, and 58 people were injured," said aid worker Wai Hun Aung on Tuesday, warning the final fatality figure may be higher because some bodies were lost in fires after the bombing.
A second local volunteer gave the same death toll, requesting anonymity for security reasons.
The Arakan Army (AA) – a local ethnic rebel force controlling the area – said in a statement that those killed were "innocent passersby, market vendors, shoppers and cargo loaders."
It also reported that 50 people died.
Families gathered in the area to claim bodies covered by thin plastic sheeting or boxed up in plywood coffins under an outdoor pavilion.
"I don't know where to find his body and whom we should ask for help," said Aung Chay.
The market and adjacent bridge hit in Monday's bombardment had become a hive of trading activity since civil war broke out in Myanmar following a 2021 military coup.
Rakhine has suffered some of the direst conditions in the war, largely cut off from the rest of Myanmar. The market thrived on a river trade route to India, which had become a lifeline.
Su Mon, a senior analyst at conflict monitor ACLED, said there have been only 10 airstrike attacks targeting civilians with more than 30 reported deaths since 2022 – the war's first full year.
"Rakhine experienced the military's mass killings the most," she said.
The AA control almost all of Rakhine, save for a few urban centres still defended by the military wielding a fleet of fighter jets manufactured by Russia and China.
The military's air wing is also accused of committing atrocities targeting civilians at schools, monasteries and religious festivals – attacks rights groups say may constitute war crimes.
"The military is eager to regain control of Rakhine," Su Mon said, launching an offensive this month which "has not yielded battlefield success."
Nearly half a million people are living displaced in Rakhine as a result of the conflict, UN data says.
More than 100,000 people have been killed in Myanmar in conflict since the 2021 putsch unseated Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government, ACLED estimates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khalid: PH-BN cooperation was never based on shared political goals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional have distinct political cultures and directions, with their cooperation in the unity government aimed solely at maintaining stability.
Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said BN's statement that its cooperation with the unity government will end once Parliament is dissolved comes as no surprise.
He noted that BN has historically been PH's political rival, with both coalitions competing in numerous elections.
"Our direction and theirs are different. We have goals and a political culture that prioritise performance and specific values, which differ significantly from Umno-BN based on their track record.
"To achieve stability following the 15th General Election (GE15), the unity government was formed despite involving two very different political entities.
"Therefore, that statement should not come as a surprise to anyone," he said when contacted today.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi recently said that BN's cooperation with the unity government will terminate upon the dissolution of Parliament.
Zahid said the commitment was a promise made to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and formalised through the
formation of the unity government
.
Addressing Umno-BN's frequent remarks regarding severing ties with PH and the unity government, Khalid said the party should exit rather than wait to be removed.
"What we see is them challenging us to fire them, but we do not act that way because it contradicts our political philosophy of seeking unity for the good of the country.
"If they truly do not want to remain, they should leave, but at the recent Umno General Assembly, there was no motion to leave — only challenges for us to dismiss them," he said.
Khalid expressed hope that Malay voters will support parties prioritising performance, service, and value-driven politics in the next general election.
"Like it or not, the choice of the Malay community will determine the government that is formed.
"If an awareness emerges — a wave demanding politics focused on performance, integrity, and values — then, Insha-Allah, a situation where no single party holds a clear majority to form a government will not recur," he said.

Title: Rapid Bus tests 5 electric buses on Sunway BRT ahead of 250-bus rollout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Prasarana Malaysia Bhd, is testing five electric buses on the Sunway Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) line ahead of the rollout of 250 new electric buses.
In a statement today, Rapid Bus said the phased procurement of the new electric buses was part of its efforts to enhance public transport services through modern, energy-efficient and sustainable technology.
"Through these trials, Rapid Bus is evaluating various aspects of electric bus performance, including energy efficiency, battery performance, driving range and charging systems, as well as passenger experience in terms of comfort, ride smoothness and noise levels," the statement said.
In addition to operational testing, Rapid Bus is also preparing for the wider adoption of electric buses, including charging infrastructure, maintenance facilities, technical training and other operational requirements.
Rapid Bus chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the trials were a crucial step towards ensuring smooth electric bus operations before the fleet was deployed on other routes.
He said the acquisition of 250 new electric buses was a significant move towards modernising the Rapid Bus fleet, improving service quality for commuters and developing a more sustainable public transport system.
"Through the trials currently underway at Sunway BRT, we can assess bus performance under real-world operating conditions and gather the necessary data before a wider rollout.
"At the same time, we want to ensure that commuters continue to enjoy safe, comfortable and reliable services," he said.
The procurement of the 250 new electric buses aligns with the company's plan to provide a more modern and sustainable public transport system that meets future mobility needs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men jailed 30 years for trafficking 139kg cannabis in Bangsar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two parcel delivery men were sentenced to 30 years in jail and 12 strokes of the rotan each by the High Court today after they were found guilty of trafficking 139kg of cannabis in 2022.
Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin sentenced S. Mohan, 38, and Ahmad Shamil Abdul Rashid, 28, after ruling that the prosecution had proven its case beyond a reasonable doubt.
"After considering all the facts, evidence from the witnesses and submissions from both parties, I find that the prosecution has proven its case beyond a reasonable doubt against both accused.
"I find both accused guilty. The jail sentences are to run from their arrest on May 31, 2022," he said.
The duo, who stood in the dock, appeared calm and composed after the decision was delivered.
Their friends, who had been seated in the public gallery since this morning, returned to the courtroom after the lunch break to hear the verdict.
Mohan and Ahmad Shamil were charged with jointly trafficking 139,019.3 grammes of cannabis a shopping complex car park in Bangsar about 2pm on May 31, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act and read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
Section 39B provides for the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of not less than 12 strokes upon conviction.
During mitigation, lawyer Mohamed Yazzer Azzad Zainudin, representing Mohan, said his client was a bachelor and had been in custody since his arrest on May 31, 2022.
"He regrets the incident and the period he has spent in remand has truly given him an opportunity to repent. He is also supporting his 57-year-old mother. I humbly ask the court to impose a custodial sentence," he said.
Lawyer Muhammad Faiz Fadzil, representing Ahmad Shamil, said his client had also been in custody since his arrest.
"This is my client's first offence. The period he has spent in remand has given him an opportunity to repent and we hope this will allow him to lead a better life and reform himself in the future," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Zaileen Nadia Zubir urged the court to take into consideration the nature and quantity of the drugs involved.
"The 139kg of cannabis constitutes a substantial amount.
"The manner in which the drugs were transferred and transported is also an unusual modus operandi," she said.
According to the facts of the case, a raiding team from the Selangor police contingent headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department conducted surveillance at the car park from an unmarked police vehicle.
The team spotted a Proton Preve and a Toyota Vellfire parked side by side.
Police observed Mohan alighting from the Proton Preve and walking towards the rear of the Toyota Vellfire, while Ahmad Shamil alighted from the Vellfire and also went to its rear.
No one else was in either vehicle.
Two prosecution witnesses then saw both men handling and transferring several plastic packets or bags from the Toyota Vellfire into the Proton Preve.
The raiding officer then instructed his team to apprehend the accused.
However, Ahmad Shamil, who was driving the Toyota Vellfire, managed to leave the car park. A car chase ensued, with Ahmad Shamil eventually arrested by police at the roadside along Jalan Telawi 1.
The arresting officer testified that Ahmad Shamil appeared shocked and remained silent when he was arrested before being taken back to the car park.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor RTD investigates foreigners renting cars to operate 'kereta sapu' services
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor Road Transport Department (RTD) is investigating allegations that foreigners were renting cars from Malaysians and using them to operate illegal e-hailing and "kereta sapu" services in several districts in the state.
The investigation followed a viral video showing a man believed to be a Bangladeshi picking up passengers near a bus terminal in a district in the state.
The clip also showed a Malaysian confronting the foreign driver, who was allegedly driving a vehicle without a valid driving licence, e-hailing permit and road tax.
Johor RTD director Zulkarnain Yasin said the department had received the complaint and called the complainant to obtain more details.
"We are yet to confirm whether the vehicle featured in the footage was used for illegal e-hailing or whether the driver was operating without the required licences," he told the New Straits Times.
He said RTD had issued a notice under Section 114 of the Road Transport Act 1987 to the registered owner of the vehicle, requiring the person to appear at the department to facilitate investigations.
"If the vehicle owner fails to appear, a summons will be issued for failing to comply with the notice. The offence carries a maximum compound of RM300 and, upon conviction in court, a fine of up to RM2,000," he said.
Zulkarnain said action would be taken against the driver and vehicle owner if investigations established that offences had been committed.
"For example, if the investigation involves a road tax offence, both the driver and vehicle owner may be issued summonses requiring them to settle the matter in court.
"If convicted, each may face a fine of up to RM2,000," he said.
He added that driving without a valid licence carries a fine of between RM300 and  RM2,000.
The footage, which was uploaded on TikTok, claimed that foreigners were providing illegal passenger transport services in several parts of Johor.
Commonly known as "kereta sapu", the vehicles are believed to be used as unlicensed private taxis, with the foreigners allegedly charging passengers between RM5 and RM50, depending on the distance.
Each vehicle is said to carry up to five passengers, with fares collected individually.
The service also raises safety and liability concerns, as passengers travelling in such vehicles may not be covered by valid insurance for commercial passenger transport in the event of an accident.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards call Trump a 'big liar'
Article:
DUBAI: Iran's Revolutionary Guards' spokesperson said on Tuesday Donald Trump was a "big liar", citing the US president's statements on nuclear weapons and other issues.
"The American people need to be told the truth," Hossein Mohebbi said, adding that the US had failed in its military campaign against Iran and should leave the region.
Meanwhile, Iran's parliamentary speaker said that no country in the region would be able to export oil if the Islamic Republic was prevented from selling its own oil, state media reported.'
No regional infrastructure would be safe if Iran had no security, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf added, according to the reports.
Ghalibaf also said that if his country's security was not guaranteed, no infrastructure in the region would be safe from attack, state media reported.
"In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe," said Ghalibaf, who is also Iran's parliament speaker, according to video released by state TV.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH rules out cooperation with BN for Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan will not partner with Barisan Nasional for the upcoming 16th Melaka election.
Amanah communications director Khalid Abdul Samad said PH has decided on the matter and remains open to collaborating with any other party except BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN).
"We will not accept any offer to align with BN. If BN wishes to work with PN, that is their right and entirely up to them.
"As for PH, we will contest based on the principles we uphold," he said when contacted today.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari previously called on BN to clarify its stance regarding potential cooperation for the Melaka polls following a lack of progress in talks between both sides.
Senior PH and Bersatu leaders met at a closed-door event in Melaka last night, believed to be aimed at discussing electoral cooperation for the state polls.
At the same time, BN is expected to meet with several party coalitions this week to negotiate a political understanding for the election.
Commenting on potential cooperation between PH and Bersatu, Khalid, who is also a former Federal Territories minister, said Bersatu must understand PH's principles, which emphasise performance, integrity, and values.
"When forming a pre-election alignment, these are the matters we discuss. We have options and can lay down necessary conditions and assertions.
"If they agree, we can work with Bersatu, Muda, and other parties not aligned with BN and PN.
"However, post-election scenarios may differ if no coalition reaches a majority, forcing a joint pact," he said.
On seat allocations for the Melaka election, Khalid said negotiations among PH component parties have been completed and will be announced once the Election Commission sets the election date.
"If new partners join, they will negotiate directly with the designated component party contesting those respective seats," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smart lights to respond to Kulai traffic in real time
Article:
KULAI:  Motorists in Indahpura could soon spend less time waiting at traffic lights as Kulai Municipal Council trials a smart traffic system designed to adjust signal timings according to real-time traffic conditions.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the system was being trialled at the Bandar Putra-Indahpura interchange, with its effectiveness to be measured by how much it could reduce journey times and vehicle queues.
"The measure of success is simple — if people spend less time waiting, face shorter queues and reach their destinations faster, then the technology is delivering real benefits," he said after inspecting its implementation with Kulai Municipal Council officials on Sunday.
The system uses Virtual Loop technology, sensors and intelligent controls to detect actual traffic demand and adjust signal timings according to the number of vehicles using each lane.
Unlike conventional fixed-time signals, it can give priority to busier approaches while reducing waiting times for lanes with little or no traffic.
Jafni said the system could also coordinate signals between junctions to improve traffic flow across multiple intersections, while its operation could be monitored in real time through the Kulai Integrated Command, Control and Communication Centre.
Countdown timers have also been installed alongside the Virtual Loop system to help motorists anticipate when traffic signals will change.
Phase One covers six locations in Kulai, with five already equipped with the system. The Bandar Putra-Indahpura interchange is among the upgraded locations.
Jafni said the next stage would focus on measuring actual results, including reductions in journey times and vehicle queues, rather than merely confirming that the system was technically operational.
"After the trial, what we want to see is the data — how much journey time has been reduced, how much queues have been shortened and what difference the system makes to motorists every day," he said.
Phase Two will cover seven more junctions and is scheduled for completion by December, including the Persiaran 1, Indahpura/FT1 intersection.
Jafni said the phased approach would allow each system to be tested and fine-tuned based on actual traffic conditions before wider implementation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retired soldier fined RM4,000 for false birth registration
Article:
KUANTAN: A retired soldier was fined RM4,000 by the magistrate's court after pleading guilty to providing false information when registering his child's birth 19 years ago.
Mohd Fauzi Samsir, 60, pleaded guilty after the charge was read to him before magistrate Ellyana Othman.
He was charged with providing false information when filling out a birth registration form, resulting in the issuance of a birth certificate for the child.
The offence was committed at the Birth, Death and Adoption Division counter of the Pahang National Registration Department at 4.47pm on Dec 4, 2007.
He was charged under Section 36(1)(b) of the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957, which provides for a maximum fine of RM20,000, imprisonment of up to three years, or both upon conviction.
Fauzi submitted the birth registration form for his child, along with the maternal health record book, at the registaration department's counter on Dec 4, 2007.
A DNA profiling analysis conducted last year found that the child was not biologically related to his wife.
Fauzi was told to report to the office here yesterday, where he was detained for questioning.
The court also ordered seven months' imprisonment if Fauzi failed to pay the fine. He has since paid the fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CAAM: Don't be alarmed by low-flying aircraft over Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public has been advised not to be alarmed by low-flying aircraft over the Sepang International Circuit and surrounding areas from tomorrow to Sunday in conjunction with the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 in Malaysia.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the operations would take place between 2pm and 3pm on the scheduled dates, with aircraft expected to fly at lower altitudes than usual.
"Operations have been coordinated with the relevant authorities and will be conducted in accordance with applicable safety requirements," it said in a statement.
CAAM also reminded drone operators that unauthorised flights are prohibited in the affected airspace, warning that drones pose a serious risk to low-flying aircraft and people on the ground.
"Drone operators must obtain the necessary authorisation before conducting any flight, while those operating without authorisation could face investigation and enforcement action under the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016 and other applicable laws.
"The public and drone operators are advised to comply with the restrictions and cooperate with the relevant authorities to ensure the safe conduct of the aircraft operations," it said.
Earlier, CAAM deputy chief executive officer Zainul Abidin Maslan said a low-level flypast by a Gulf Air Boeing 787 Dreamliner was expected to wow crowds at the race.
Zainul said the flypast had been coordinated between CAAM's air traffic control centre and the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) control tower.

Title: Over 100 settlers attack West Bank village, injuring Israeli forces
Article:
RAMALLAH: More than 100 Israeli settlers attacked a village in the north of the occupied West Bank early Tuesday, wounding three members of Israel's security forces and burning two Palestinian homes, authorities and residents said.
The attack occurred while the military was attempting to accompany a Palestinian family back to their home in the village of Jalud after they had been displaced by settler attacks two months earlier.
Tuesday's assault received rare strong criticism from Israeli officials, while police said they had arrested one individual and taken two minors in for questioning.
The Israeli military said "more than 100 Israeli rioters" were in the area of Jalud overnight as security forces attempted to return the family to their home, adding that soldiers and border police forces had operated to disperse the settlers.
"As a result of the clashes, three Israel Border Police officers were lightly injured, and a security forces vehicle was damaged," it said in a statement.
The military said the settlers had blocked roads, set tyres on fire and thrown rocks at security forces, as well as setting fire to Palestinian buildings and vehicles in the village.
It added that the attack had prevented the return of the family, who had been displaced "following several incidents of (Israeli) nationalist crime against them."
Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, where 500,000 Israeli settlers live among three million Palestinians.
[[nid:1543859]]
Mahmoud al-Toubasi, a member of the family, told AFP that he and his relatives had left the house over two months ago, and that it had been occupied by settlers until the attack on Tuesday.
"My wife, my son and I went to the house in the car, accompanied by an army vehicle in front of us and another behind us," he said.
Settlers attacked the group upon their arrival at the house and were pushed back by soldiers with pepper spray, he added.
"We were not physically injured, but we suffered some choking from the pepper spray," said Toubasi.
Israel's police said they had arrested one suspect and taken two minors in for questioning.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the attack, which he blamed on a "small group of rioters."
He said "their actions cause great harm to that community and interfere with our forces as they carry out their mission."
President Isaac Herzog said "the arson, stone-throwing, assault, and injury of IDF soldiers and Border Police officers... are strictly forbidden and can have no justification whatsoever."
Violence has increased in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023, with Israeli soldiers or settlers killing at least 1,111 Palestinians in that period, including both fighters and civilians, per an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry.
Israeli figures show at least 49 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations during the same period.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gulf Air Dreamliner flypast to wow F1 crowds at Sepang
Article:
SEPANG: A low-level flypast by a Gulf Air Boeing 787 Dreamliner is expected to wow crowds at the Sepang International Circuit as the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026 gets underway on Sunday.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) deputy chief executive officer Zainul Abidin Maslan said the flypast had been coordinated between CAAM's Air Traffic Control Centre and the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) control tower.
"There will be a low-level flypast just as the race flags off. That has been coordinated by both the Kuala Lumpur Air Traffic Control Centre and the KLIA control tower.
"It will cause minimal disruption to air traffic. But we are also ready to accommodate that kind of operation during race day," he said at a media engagement programme hosted by CAAM and the Malaysian Press Institute.
Zainul said the Gulf Air Boeing 787 Dreamliner was scheduled to conduct a rehearsal flypast between 2.45pm and 3pm tomorrow, ahead of the actual flypast on Sunday.
He added that CAAM was also prepared to manage additional flights arriving ahead of the grand prix weekend.
"The additional flights carrying Formula 1 logistics and teams have been taken into consideration, with air traffic controllers prepared to manage the operations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail Lasim leaves palace after three-hour audience with Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim concluded a nearly three-hour audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap here today.
Ismail, who arrived at 10.50am for the 11am audience, left the palace grounds via the back gate, avoiding media members gathered outside.
The session is believed to be linked to the ongoing palace and custom crisis in the state.
Vehicles carrying Rembau Undang Hassan Ab Hamid and Sungei Ujong Undang Muhammad Faris Johari were seen leaving the palace at 1.48pm.
Hassan lowered his window to wave at media personnel, stating that discussions had yet to conclude.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad, who was also present, declined to comment further, describing the session as confidential.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had previously directed Ismail to seek an audience with Tuanku Muhriz to address the ongoing custom crisis.
Zahid, who is also the Umno president, said an optimal solution must be found at the state level to prevent further complications and protect public interest.

Title: Serian tops API readings as 33 areas record unhealthy levels

Title: Tokyo suffers longest streak of rainy days on record
Article:
TOKYO: Tokyo has logged 34 straight days of rain, marking the longest streak on record, Japan's weather agency said on Tuesday.
Climate change fuelled by fossil fuel emissions increases moisture in the atmosphere, making heavy rain more likely.
The weather globally is also being shaped this year by the El Nino phenomenon, which shifts winds, air pressure and cloud patterns and can bring heavy rain to some areas and droughts elsewhere.
The Japanese capital's rainy season is normally in June, but it has suffered regular heavy downpours throughout the summer months, as well as heavy flooding in the wider Tokyo region.
The stretch of rainy days was the longest since records began in 1886.
Masayuki Kyoda, an official at the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), told AFP that "the distinctive weather map during this month is in part because of El Nino", bringing higher temperatures in the Pacific Ocean.
"Autumn rain fronts are staying longer than usual," Kyoda said, referring to Tokyo's rainy season, because a high pressure system in the Pacific is also remaining longer than normal.
He said that although it was not possible to directly link the streak to climate change, a JMA report last year concluded that "global warming was impacting Japan's weather long-term, including through more precipitation."
The previous record of the longest streak of rainy days in Tokyo was 33 between June 27 and Sept 29, 2019, said Kazuhiro Hirono, another JMA official.
The Mainichi Shimbun daily reported that central Tokyo had been soaked by 629 millimetres of rain in September through to Monday, nearly three times the normal level.
That was approaching the September record of 670.9 millimetres set in 1958.
Tokyo's wet weather comes as 1.7 million people were affected by recent flooding in Thailand after an intense weather system hit the region, with 23 people killed since mid-September.
